cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest among the exiles by the River Kebar (Ezekiel 1:1-3), and the word of the LORD comes to him again. God calls him son of man and tells him to set his face against Mount Seir, where Esau, also called Edom, settled (Genesis 36:8). Ezekiel has to stare down a whole MOUNTAIN, friend, and I once lost a staring contest to a dead battery in the junk drawer I was stuck in for years.
Here's what God tells him to declare: "Behold, I am against you, O Mount Seir."

cards.question: God says He'll stretch out His hand against Mount Seir. What will He make it?
God says that when Mount Seir's cities are turned into ruins, Seir will know that He is the LORD.

cards.text: Now God gives the reason, and it goes way back. Mount Seir harbored an ancient hatred.

cards.question: Mount Seir harbored an ancient hatred. What did it do to the Israelites in the time of their disaster?

answers.text: Handed them over to the sword

cards.text: Then God says, "…as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will give you over to bloodshed…"

cards.question: Mount Seir did not hate bloodshed. So God says bloodshed will ___ Seir.

cards.text: God says He will make Mount Seir a desolate waste and cut off those who come and go. He will fill its hills, valleys and ravines with those killed by the sword.

cards.question: God says Mount Seir will be desolate for a while, and then its cities will be lived in again.

cards.text: Then God gives a second reason. Seir said those two nations and countries would be theirs, and they would possess them.

cards.question: Mount Seir said those two nations and countries would be its own. But God points out a problem. What is it?

cards.text: Friend, that's calling dibs on the couch while the owner is sitting ON the couch. So God says it again: as surely as He lives, He'll treat Seir according to the anger and jealousy it showed in its hatred against them.
And God says Seir will know He heard every contemptuous word it uttered against the mountains of Israel, like "They are desolate; they are given to us to devour!" Every. Single. Word.

cards.question: Mount Seir kept running its mouth about Israel's mountains. Who does God say Seir was really boasting against?
God says that while the whole earth ___, He will make Mount Seir desolate.

cards.text: Seir rejoiced when the inheritance of the house of Israel became desolate. And God says, "…so will I do to you."

cards.question: God's word against Mount Seir reaches past one mountain: all of Edom will become a desolation too.

cards.text: Same prophet, new mountains: God tells Ezekiel to prophesy to the mountains of Israel. The enemy had said of them, "Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession," and God has something to say about that.

cards.question: God says Israel's mountains were trampled on every side.

cards.text: So God speaks to every corner of the land: its mountains and hills, ravines and valleys, ruins and abandoned cities, all mocked by the nations around. In His burning zeal, He has spoken against the rest of the nations and against all Edom.

cards.question: God says Edom took His land as its own possession with wholehearted joy and utter contempt, so that its pastureland became ___.

cards.text: God says He has spoken in His burning zeal because Israel's mountains have endured the reproach of the nations. Then He swears with an uplifted hand.

cards.question: What does God swear will happen to the nations around Israel's mountains?

answers.text: They will endure reproach of their own
They will rule over the mountains forever
They will be left completely untouched

cards.text: And now the whole message turns on one little word: "But you, O mountains of Israel…" Friend, I'm leaning in so far I almost tipped over, gold base and all.

cards.question: God turns to the mountains of Israel. What does He say those mountains will do?
God says His people Israel will soon come home.

cards.text: To Mount Seir, God said, "Behold, I am against you, O Mount Seir." To the mountains of Israel, same "behold," COMPLETELY different news: "For behold, I am on your side…"

cards.question: God says He will turn toward the mountains of Israel. What will happen to the land?

answers.text: It will be tilled and sown
It will be fenced and guarded
It will be left to rest

cards.text: And God will multiply the people on those mountains, the house of Israel in its entirety. Not a few stragglers, friend, EVERYBODY.

cards.question: God says the cities of Israel will be inhabited and the ruins ___.
God promises to make Israel's mountains as inhabited as they once were. What else does He promise?

answers.text: To make them prosper more than before
To let them prosper for a season
To keep them small and quiet

cards.text: Back to how it was AND then some, like getting your old job back with a RAISE. God will cause His people Israel to walk on these mountains and possess them as their inheritance.
But people say to this land, "You devour men and deprive your nation of its children," and now God answers it.

cards.question: People say the land of Israel devours men. God declares that the land will keep on devouring men.
God makes one more promise to the mountains of Israel. What will He no longer allow to be heard against them?
